title: Block entropy area based non-local fermionic mode optimization with gradient disentanglers
authors: Miklós Antal Werner, Gero Friesecke, Andor Menczer, Kornél Kapás, Örs Legeza
abstract: We introduce a systematic block entropy area based mode optimization algorithm for many-body quantum states of interacting fermions represented by matrix product states. From the gradient of a global cost function, the block entropy area, a long-ranged, non-interacting effective disentangler Hamiltonian is formed. We then simulate the time-dependent Schrödinger equation driven by the disentangler Hamiltonian by employing the time-dependent variational principle based on projector splitting, and minimize the cost function. The combination of the density matrix renormalization group with this gradient-based entanglement minimization forms an efficient low-rank iterative ground-state algorithm that also provides an optimized single-particle basis for matrix product state representation. We demonstrate the method on two-dimensional lattice models of interacting fermions and the Fe${_4}$S${_4}$ cluster, and show its robustness and superiority over earlier protocols using nearest-neighbor mode rotations and reorderings.
summary: This paper presents a novel, gradient-based algorithm (gradBEA) to optimize the single-particle basis used in Matrix Product States for fermionic systems. By minimizing a block entropy area cost function, the method iteratively refines the state representation, achieving superior convergence and accuracy compared to previous local optimization techniques. It provides a powerful, generalizable tool for simulating complex quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The core problem is efficiently finding the ground state eigenstates of many-body Hamiltonians for interacting fermions, which is computationally intractable due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space.
main_result: The proposed gradient-based method (gradBEA) achieves significantly faster convergence and yields lower ground state energies compared to established local optimization protocols.
method: It introduces a systematic block entropy area based mode optimization algorithm that uses the gradient of an entanglement cost function to drive an iterative, non-local update of the single-particle basis within the Matrix Product State framework.
model_or_system: The method is applied to interacting fermions, modeled using Matrix Product States (MPS). Specific examples include spinless 'tt'V' models on a square lattice, the Hubbard model, and the $	ext{Fe}_4	ext{S}_4$ cluster.
key_observables: The primary observables are the ground state energy ($E_0/t$) and the entanglement measure, the block entropy area ($B_\mu$).
important_parameters: The optimization depends on the entanglement measure ($\mu$-Rényi entropy $S^{(i)}_\mu$) and the parameters ($\vec{	heta}$) governing the unitary rotations ($U^{(s)}$).
main_assumptions: The optimization is performed iteratively by following the steepest descent path defined by the gradient, and the method is restricted to optimizing rotations within the spanned single-particle space.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the ground state energy convergence of gradBEA against local methods for the $	ext{tt}'	ext{V}$ model. Figure 2 illustrates the iterative loop and the tensor diagram used in the calculation.
paper_structure: The paper details the systematic derivation of the gradient of the block entropy area, outlines the three-step iterative optimization protocol (DMRG simulation, gradient calculation, time evolution via PS-TDVP), and validates the method on various lattice and molecular models.
why_interesting: The development of a non-local, gradient-based optimization technique for tensor network representations is a powerful algorithmic advance for simulating strongly correlated quantum systems, potentially improving upon standard DMRG limitations.
